div.head: VI As 6.1
div.ab: Syxte, émban urne ceapgild: hors to healfan punde, gif hit swa gód sy; ⁊ gif hit mætre sy, gilde be his wlites wyrðe ⁊ be þam þe se man hit weorðige þe hit áge, buton he gewitnesse habbe, þæt hit swa god wære swa he secge; ⁊ habbe þone oferéacan, þe we þar abiddan.

Sextum, de nostro ceapgildo (id est de nostro captali persoluendo): equus X solid., si tam bonus sit. Si sit metre (betre, id est melior), reddatur secundum pretium appreciatum et sicut ille comprobabit cuius erit, nisi testes habeat, quod tanti ualens fuit, sicut dicit; et habeamus nobis superplus, sicut ante constituimus.

Syxte: Émban ure ceapgild: hors to healfan punde, gif hit swa gód sy; ⁊ gif hit mætre sy, gilde be his wlites wyrðe ⁊ be þam þe se man hit weorðige þe hit áge, buton he gewitnesse habbe, þæt hit swa god wære swa he secge; ⁊ habbe þone oferéacan þe we þar abiddan.

Sechstens: betreffend unser Ersatzgeld [an bestohlene Genossen]: ein Pferd [schätzen wir höchstens] zu einem halben Pfund, wenn es so werthvoll ist; und wenn es geringer ist, zahlen wir je nach Werth seiner Beschaffenheit, und zwar je nachdem der Mann, dem es gehört, es [eidlich] bewerthet, ausser wenn er [statt Eides] Zeugniss hat, dass es so gut war, wie er behauptet; und mögen (wir für uns Quadr.) den Überschuss behalten, den wir dabei [gerichtlich] erlangen.

Sixthly: concerning our compensation-money [to fellow-members who have been robbed]: a horse [we value at most] at half a pound, if it is so valuable; and if it is of less value, we pay according to the worth of its condition, and namely according as the man to whom it belongs values it [on oath], unless he has witness [instead of an oath] that it was as good as he claims; and let (us, Quadr.) keep the surplus that we obtain [in court] from it.

Sixth: With reference to indemnities for livestock, we reckon a horse at half a pound, if it is worth so much; but if it is less valuable it shall be paid for according to the value suggested by its appearance, and what is approved by its owner, unless he can produce evidence that it is as good a horse as he says; in that case he shall have such additional sum as we are awarded in the suit.

Sixthly: concerning our compensation, a horse [is to be paid for] with half a pound, if it is worth so much, and if it is inferior it is to be paid for according to its value, judging by its appearance, and to the value the owner sets on it, unless he has witness that it was as good as he says; and he is to have the additional payment that we obtain there.

div.note: H's ‘urne’ is corrected to ‘ure’ by Price and his followers; Liebermann would supply ‘we’ (or ‘man’) before ‘gilde’ and ‘we (us?)’ after ‘habbe’ from Quadr.

note.seg: ure emended by Price and following edd.
ergänze we oder, laut Quadr., man
supply we or, according to Quadr., man
so Lond; solu. c. [capit. T stets] n. übrige
thus Lond; solu. c. [capit. T throughout] n. the others
nur K (ohne b. i. m.); fehlt übrigen
only K (without b. i. m.); lacking in the others
Mittelengl. Wechsel des Genus? s. d. Wb 3
Middle English change of gender? see that word in Wb 3
nicht, wie Q meint, das vom Diebe (Prozessgegner) zu Zahlende, sondern das von der Gilde dem einzelnen durch sie versicherten Genossen zu Ersetzende
not, as Q thinks, what is to be paid by the thief (the opposing party), but what is to be made good by the guild to the individual member insured by it
Q versetzt die Rechnung des Schilling (s. d. Gl 7) zu 1/20 Pfund irrig schon ins 10. Jh. hinauf, auch 6, 3f.
Q wrongly carries the reckoning of the shilling (see that word in Gl 7) as 1/20 of a pound back as early as the 10th cent., also at 6, 3f.
Q verstand mætre nicht mehr und änderte in 2. Rez. falsch aus ähnlichem Klang; er fand also betre nicht in der Vorlage; man darf dies nicht H mit Price vorziehen
Q no longer understood mætre and in his 2nd recension wrongly altered it on the basis of a similar sound; he therefore did not find betre in his exemplar; it must not be preferred to H, as Price does
Über diese Form (beode we 8, 8) vgl. Sievers Gram. § 360, 2. Eine Ellipse des man, früher möglich, ist diesem Sprachzeitalter um 935 nicht mehr zuzutrauen
On this form (beode we 8, 8) cf. Sievers Gram. § 360, 2. An ellipsis of man, possible earlier, can no longer be expected in this period of the language, c. 935

Thorpe und Schmid ergänzen ne, so dass objektiver Wert gegen Schätzung des Bestohlenen stehe. Vielmehr ist Eid des Letzteren die eine Art der Werterweisung (s. Gl Taxe 7), Zeugnis die andere, leichtere

Thorpe and Schmid supply ne, so that objective value would stand in contrast to the valuation of the man robbed. Rather, the latter's oath is one way of proving value (see Gl Taxe 7), testimony the other, easier one
hier war we vielleicht Ellipse des Originals, ergänzbar aus o. Erkl. 6; nobis des Q ist sinngemäss, vielleicht aus originalem Dativus ethicus, konnte aber fehlen
here we was perhaps an ellipsis of the original, to be supplied from above note 6; Q's nobis is true to the sense, perhaps from an original ethic dative, but could have been absent
Hier nicht ‘einfordern’; vgl. 6, 3⁸. — Q verlas wohl þe we ær abudon
Not ‘demand’ here; cf. 6, 3⁸. — Q probably misread it as þe we ær abudon

Liebermann understands ceapgild to mean here the compensation paid by the guild to one of its members who has been robbed; but in § 4, below, he takes it to mean the compensation accruing to the guild. Quadr. reads de nostro ceapgildo, id est de nostro captali persoluendo, and apparently takes ceapgild in the same sense in § 4, below.
Liebermann adds we, or following Quadr. man, as the subject of gilde. Quadr. reads Si sit metre (betre, id est melior), reddatur secundum pretium appreciatum.

Schmid (following Thorpe) and other early editors suggest- ed the insertion of ne before be þam. Liebermann accepts the emendation and translates weorðige as [eidlich] bewerthet; in the last sentence he adds ‘we’ (or ‘us’) and understands habbe to be for habben, following the reading of Quadr. (habeamus nobis superplus). The introduction of the oath (eidlich) scarcely seems to be justified by the original, and I am inclined to think that the text as it stands may be correct, although the meaning is neither clearly nor logically expressed. I would suggest that the passage be þam þe se man hit weorðige really implies some process of haggling.

note.seg: Liebermann explains this as the value he swears to by oath, in contrast to his mere statement if he has witnesses.
